- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending upward, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought traps.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price deviates >2% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast by 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is uncertain.
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and price is falling, model often ignores bearish signals; if sentiment >0.67 and price < prior low, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid false optimism.
